design_notes: The six official blocks are split into eight app topics because the event mixes calculation-heavy problem solving, mechanism interpretation, and experimental-technology analysis. Mendelian genetics is divided into single-locus Punnett/probability work versus multi-gene interaction and recombination mapping. Population/evolutionary genetics is split into Hardy-Weinberg calculations versus evolutionary/phylogenetic reasoning. DNA replication/repair, expression/regulation, and molecular technology remain separate skill chapters to keep concept maps clean. Concept counts range from 9 to 14 based on skill density; no thin topics flagged.

topics.title: Mendelian inheritance and probability
topics.why_this_topic: Students need a focused chapter for mono-, di-, and trihybrid Punnett squares, probability rules, and pedigree interpretation before adding multi-gene complications.
topics.scope_note: Includes Mendel's laws, Punnett squares, probability, pedigrees, and basic single-locus inheritance patterns; excludes linkage, epistasis, complementation, and recombination mapping.

concepts.title: Law of segregation
concepts.description: Predict allele segregation into gametes from a heterozygous parent and explain the reappearance of recessive phenotypes in F2 crosses.

concepts.title: Law of independent assortment
concepts.description: Apply independent segregation of alleles at different loci to predict gamete combinations from dihybrid or multi-locus parents.

concepts.title: Monohybrid cross genotype and phenotype ratios
concepts.description: Use a Punnett square to predict genotype and phenotype ratios for a single gene with complete dominance.

concepts.title: Dihybrid cross and 9:3:3:1 ratio
concepts.description: Predict F2 phenotypic ratios for two unlinked genes and compute the combined probability of each phenotype class.

concepts.title: Probability product and sum rules
concepts.description: Apply the product rule for independent genetic events and the sum rule for mutually exclusive outcomes in multi-child or multi-trait predictions.

concepts.title: Testcross and backcross for genotype determination
concepts.description: Determine an unknown dominant-phenotype genotype by crossing to a homozygous recessive tester and interpreting the offspring ratio.

concepts.title: Autosomal dominant pedigree interpretation
concepts.description: Diagnose autosomal dominant inheritance from affected-parent transmission, male-to-male transmission, and approximately 50% recurrence risk.

concepts.title: Autosomal recessive pedigree interpretation
concepts.description: Diagnose autosomal recessive inheritance from unaffected carrier parents, affected siblings, and consanguinity clues.

concepts.title: X-linked recessive pedigree interpretation
concepts.description: Diagnose X-linked recessive inheritance from affected males, carrier females, and absence of male-to-male transmission in a pedigree.

concepts.title: Pedigree carrier and recurrence probability
concepts.description: Calculate carrier or recurrence probabilities in pedigrees by multiplying prior genotype risks and conditional probabilities from pedigree structure.

concepts.title: Chi-square test for Mendelian ratios
concepts.description: Perform a chi-square goodness-of-fit test comparing observed offspring counts to expected Mendelian ratios and interpret p-values and degrees of freedom.

topics.title: Gene interactions and linkage mapping
topics.why_this_topic: Non-Mendelian inheritance patterns and recombination-based mapping require a separate interpretative and calculation skill set from single-locus Punnett problems.
topics.scope_note: Includes linkage, incomplete/codominance, complementation, epistasis, and gene mapping by recombination frequency; excludes population-level Hardy-Weinberg calculations.

concepts.title: Incomplete dominance and intermediate phenotype
concepts.description: Predict 1:2:1 phenotypic and genotypic ratios when a heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype rather than full dominance.

concepts.title: Codominance and multiple alleles
concepts.description: Use codominant alleles and multiple-allele systems such as ABO blood groups to determine possible parental and offspring genotypes/phenotypes.

concepts.title: Lethal alleles and modified ratios
concepts.description: Identify lethal allele genotypes that distort Mendelian ratios, such as 2:1 instead of 3:1, and explain the missing phenotypic class.

concepts.title: Linkage and parental vs recombinant gametes
concepts.description: Distinguish linked from unlinked genes by comparing parental and recombinant gamete or progeny classes in a dihybrid testcross.

concepts.title: Recombination frequency and map units
concepts.description: Calculate recombination frequency from progeny counts and convert it to map distance in centimorgans.

concepts.title: Two-point testcross mapping
concepts.description: Use a two-point testcross to infer linkage and estimate map distance between two genes, recognizing that it cannot determine gene order relative to other loci.

concepts.title: Three-point testcross and double crossover
concepts.description: Analyze a three-point testcross to identify parental, single-crossover, and double-crossover progeny and determine gene order and intergenic distances.

concepts.title: Interference and coefficient of coincidence
concepts.description: Calculate coefficient of coincidence and interference from observed versus expected double crossovers in three-point crosses.

concepts.title: Epistasis and modified dihybrid ratios
concepts.description: Interpret modified dihybrid F2 ratios such as 9:3:4, 12:3:1, and 9:7 as epistatic interactions and identify the masked phenotypic class.

concepts.title: Complementation test
concepts.description: Use complementation crosses to determine whether two recessive mutations with the same phenotype are alleles of the same gene or of different genes.

concepts.title: Penetrance and expressivity
concepts.description: Distinguish incomplete penetrance from variable expressivity and adjust expected phenotype frequencies using percent penetrance.

topics.title: Mitosis, meiosis, and chromosome dynamics
topics.why_this_topic: Cell division stages, chromosome abnormalities, and specialized DNA rearrangements form a coherent chromosome-behavior chapter distinct from molecular replication and expression.
topics.scope_note: Includes mitotic/meiotic stages and structures, nondisjunction, karyotypes, and V(D)J/class-switch recombination as specialized chromosome/DNA rearrangement; excludes DNA replication/repair and gene expression regulation.

concepts.title: Cell cycle phases and checkpoints
concepts.description: Relate G1/S, G2/M, and spindle checkpoints to control of cell division and prevention of genome instability.

concepts.title: Mitosis stages and spindle behavior
concepts.description: Order prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase by chromosome condensation, spindle attachment, and sister chromatid separation.

concepts.title: Meiosis I synapsis and crossing over
concepts.description: Describe homologous chromosome pairing, synaptonemal complex formation, chiasmata, and crossing over during prophase I and reductional division.

concepts.title: Meiosis II and gamete ploidy
concepts.description: Explain how sister chromatid separation in meiosis II produces haploid gametes and contrast the equational division with meiosis I.

concepts.title: Nondisjunction in meiosis I vs meiosis II
concepts.description: Predict gamete chromosome complements when nondisjunction occurs in meiosis I versus meiosis II and connect these to aneuploid zygote outcomes.

concepts.title: Aneuploidy syndromes and karyotype interpretation
concepts.description: Read human karyotypes to diagnose trisomy 21, Turner syndrome, Klinefelter syndrome, and other aneuploidies from chromosome number and sex chromosome composition.

concepts.title: Chromosome morphology and banding
concepts.description: Identify centromeres, telomeres, p/q arms, and G-bands, and classify chromosomes as metacentric, submetacentric, or acrocentric.

concepts.title: Spermatogenesis and oogenesis
concepts.description: Compare timing, meiotic arrest points, and cell products of male and female gametogenesis.

concepts.title: V(D)J recombination
concepts.description: Explain somatic recombination of V, D, and J gene segments and junctional diversity in generating antibody and T-cell receptor diversity.

concepts.title: Class switch recombination
concepts.description: Distinguish class switch recombination from V(D)J recombination and relate it to switching immunoglobulin heavy-chain constant region genes such as IgM to IgG.

topics.title: Population genetics and Hardy-Weinberg
topics.why_this_topic: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and evolutionary forces are calculation- and model-heavy, so they need a dedicated quantitative chapter separate from phylogenetic interpretation.
topics.scope_note: Includes allele/genotype frequencies, Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, drift, founder/bottleneck effects, migration, and fitness; excludes phylogenetics and molecular homology concepts.

concepts.title: Allele and genotype frequency calculation
concepts.description: Calculate allele frequencies from genotype counts and convert allele frequencies to expected genotype frequencies under random mating.

concepts.title: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumptions
concepts.description: List and explain the Hardy-Weinberg assumptions: no mutation, random mating, no gene flow, large population, and no selection.

concepts.title: Hardy-Weinberg equation
concepts.description: Use p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1 to compute expected genotype frequencies from allele frequencies and identify the heterozygote class.

concepts.title: Carrier frequency from autosomal recessive incidence
concepts.description: Calculate carrier frequency approximately 2q for an autosomal recessive condition from disease incidence q^2 under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

concepts.title: Chi-square test for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
concepts.description: Test whether observed population genotype counts match Hardy-Weinberg expectations using chi-square and interpret disequilibrium.

concepts.title: Genetic drift and effective population size
concepts.description: Explain random allele-frequency change in finite populations and use effective population size to predict heterozygosity loss per generation.

concepts.title: Founder effect
concepts.description: Describe how a small founding population samples allele frequencies nonrepresentatively and can elevate rare disease allele frequency.

concepts.title: Population bottleneck effect
concepts.description: Explain how a population size crash reduces genetic diversity and alters allele frequencies independently of selection.

concepts.title: Gene flow and migration
concepts.description: Predict how migration between populations homogenizes allele frequencies and can introduce new alleles or change genotype frequencies.

concepts.title: Relative fitness and natural selection
concepts.description: Use relative fitness coefficients and selection coefficients to predict allele frequency change under directional, stabilizing, and balancing selection.

concepts.title: Inbreeding coefficient and nonrandom mating
concepts.description: Interpret the inbreeding coefficient F as reduction in heterozygosity and calculate genotype frequencies under nonrandom mating.

topics.title: Evolutionary genetics and quantitative traits
topics.why_this_topic: Phylogenetic reasoning, gene duplication/homology, and continuous variation form an evolutionary-interpretation chapter that is tested differently from Hardy-Weinberg calculations.
topics.scope_note: Includes additive alleles, continuous variation, heritability, gene duplication, homologs/orthologs/paralogs, and phylogenies; excludes population allele-frequency equilibrium calculations.

concepts.title: Continuous vs discontinuous variation
concepts.description: Distinguish continuous polygenic traits from discrete Mendelian trait classes and explain environmental contribution to phenotypic variance.

concepts.title: Additive allele model for polygenic traits
concepts.description: Predict phenotypic classes and frequencies for polygenic traits under an additive allele model using binomial expansion.

concepts.title: Broad-sense and narrow-sense heritability
concepts.description: Define broad-sense H2 = Vg/Vp and narrow-sense h2 = Va/Vp and explain what each variance component measures.

concepts.title: Breeder's equation and response to selection
concepts.description: Use R = h2 S to predict response to selection from heritability and selection differential.

concepts.title: Gene duplication and evolutionary fates
concepts.description: Explain neofunctionalization, subfunctionalization, and pseudogenization as possible fates of duplicated genes.

concepts.title: Homologs, orthologs, and paralogs
concepts.description: Distinguish homologous genes from orthologs produced by speciation and paralogs produced by duplication, and use them to infer evolutionary relationships.

concepts.title: Phylogenetic tree interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret rooted trees, identify monophyletic/paraphyletic/polyphyletic groups, and use synapomorphies versus symplesiomorphies.

concepts.title: Molecular clock and divergence time
concepts.description: Use substitution rates to estimate divergence times and evaluate assumptions of the neutral molecular clock.

concepts.title: Quantitative trait locus mapping
concepts.description: Interpret QTL mapping as associating marker genotypes with phenotypic variation to locate genomic regions contributing to quantitative traits.

topics.title: DNA structure, replication, and repair
topics.why_this_topic: The molecular biology of DNA is a dense, mechanism-focused block that benefits from a standalone chapter covering structure through damage responses.
topics.scope_note: Includes DNA structure/base pairing, replication forks in bacteria/archaea/eukarya, fidelity/proofreading, DNA organization, damage and repair, mutation classes, and telomeres; excludes transcription/translation and laboratory techniques.

concepts.title: Nucleotide structure and strand polarity
concepts.description: Identify nucleotide components (sugar, phosphate, nitrogenous base) and explain 5' to 3' phosphodiester bond polarity.

concepts.title: DNA double helix and Chargaff's rules
concepts.description: Relate A=T and G≡C base pairing, antiparallel strands, and major/minor groove features of B-DNA.

concepts.title: Semiconservative replication and Meselson-Stahl
concepts.description: Interpret Meselson-Stahl density-gradient bands to demonstrate semiconservative DNA replication.

concepts.title: Replication origins and bidirectional forks
concepts.description: Describe origin recognition, replication bubble formation, and bidirectional replication forks in bacterial and eukaryotic replicons.

concepts.title: Replication fork enzyme roles
concepts.description: Assign helicase, single-strand binding protein, topoisomerase, primase, DNA polymerase, and ligase to their replication fork functions.

concepts.title: Leading and lagging strand synthesis
concepts.description: Explain continuous leading strand synthesis versus discontinuous lagging strand synthesis with Okazaki fragments and RNA primers.

concepts.title: DNA polymerase proofreading and fidelity
concepts.description: Explain 3' to 5' exonuclease proofreading during DNA synthesis and how it improves replication fidelity.

concepts.title: DNA mismatch repair
concepts.description: Describe MutS/MutL/MutH mismatch repair in bacteria and how methylation distinguishes the newly synthesized strand for correction.

concepts.title: Base excision repair
concepts.description: Remove single damaged or modified bases using DNA glycosylase, AP endonuclease, and polymerase/ligase fill-in.

concepts.title: Nucleotide excision repair
concepts.description: Repair bulky DNA damage such as thymine dimers through UvrABC excinuclease in bacteria or XP-associated excision machinery in humans.

concepts.title: Double-strand break repair pathways
concepts.description: Compare homologous recombination using a sister chromatid template with error-prone nonhomologous end joining.

concepts.title: Mutation types and protein effects
concepts.description: Classify point mutations (missense, nonsense, silent), insertions/deletions, and frameshifts and predict their effects on protein sequence.

concepts.title: Telomeres and telomerase
concepts.description: Explain telomere shortening with replication, telomerase RNA-template extension, and links to senescence and cancer.

concepts.title: Eukaryotic DNA packaging and chromatin structure
concepts.description: Describe nucleosome assembly, histone octamer, H1 linker, higher-order fiber, and euchromatin versus heterochromatin organization.

topics.title: Eukaryotic gene expression and regulation
topics.why_this_topic: Central dogma, transcriptional/translational control, and regulatory elements are a distinct conceptual block from DNA replication and technology applications.
topics.scope_note: Includes central dogma, transcription, cis/trans regulators, yeast two-hybrid, RNA maturation, translation and regulation, and mobile genetic elements; excludes DNA replication/repair and PCR/sequencing methods.

concepts.title: Central dogma and reverse transcription
concepts.description: State DNA to RNA to protein information flow and recognize reverse transcription and RNA replication as exceptions.

concepts.title: RNA polymerase and promoter recognition
concepts.description: Explain RNA polymerase binding to promoter consensus sequences and the steps of transcription initiation.

concepts.title: Cis-regulatory elements and transcription factors
concepts.description: Distinguish cis-acting enhancer/silencer/promoter DNA elements from trans-acting transcription factor proteins that regulate gene expression.

concepts.title: Yeast two-hybrid assay
concepts.description: Interpret yeast two-hybrid results as evidence for direct protein-protein interactions using Gal4 DNA-binding and activation domains.

concepts.title: Eukaryotic RNA processing
concepts.description: Describe 5' capping, 3' polyadenylation, and spliceosome-mediated intron removal in pre-mRNA maturation.

concepts.title: Alternative splicing
concepts.description: Explain how alternative splice site choice generates multiple protein isoforms from one gene and the regulatory consequences of exon skipping.

concepts.title: Genetic code and tRNA wobble
concepts.description: Interpret codon tables, tRNA anticodon pairing, and wobble rules to translate mRNA sequence into amino acid order.

concepts.title: Ribosome translation steps
concepts.description: Order initiation, elongation, and termination in eukaryotic translation and identify A, P, and E site functions.

concepts.title: miRNA and translational regulation
concepts.description: Explain miRNA/siRNA-mediated translational repression or mRNA decay through RISC and seed-sequence pairing.

concepts.title: Mobile genetic elements
concepts.description: Classify DNA transposons (cut-and-paste) versus retrotransposons (copy-and-paste) and describe their mutagenic potential.

concepts.title: Chromatin modifications and transcriptional regulation
concepts.description: Relate histone acetylation and methylation and DNA methylation to transcriptional activation or silencing.

topics.title: Molecular technologies and experimental analysis
topics.why_this_topic: The event's process-heavy technology content requires a separate methods chapter focused on interpreting experimental setups, sequencing platforms, and genetic manipulation tools.
topics.scope_note: Includes PCR and applications, Illumina vs Nanopore, molecular cloning toolkit, knockout/knockdown including RNAi/Cre-Lox/CRISPR, and ChIP-seq, Hi-C, RNA-seq; excludes pure Mendelian calculations and DNA replication mechanisms.

concepts.title: PCR principle and thermal cycling
concepts.description: Describe denaturation, annealing, and extension steps of PCR and explain exponential amplification of target DNA.

concepts.title: PCR primer design and specificity
concepts.description: Design PCR primers considering length, GC content, melting temperature, and self-complementarity to avoid primer dimers and off-target products.

concepts.title: Quantitative PCR and Ct interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret real-time qPCR amplification curves and Ct/Cq values to compare starting template abundance using fluorescent detection.

concepts.title: Sanger chain-terminator sequencing
concepts.description: Interpret dideoxy chain-terminator sequencing chromatograms and distinguish Sanger from next-generation methods.

concepts.title: Illumina sequencing by synthesis
concepts.description: Explain bridge amplification, fluorescent reversible terminator chemistry, and paired-end read generation in Illumina sequencing.

concepts.title: Nanopore sequencing
concepts.description: Explain nanopore current disruption during DNA translocation and identify long-read advantages and error-profile limitations.

concepts.title: Restriction enzymes and ligation
concepts.description: Use Type II restriction recognition sites and DNA ligase to construct recombinant plasmids with compatible sticky or blunt ends.

concepts.title: Cloning vectors and transformation
concepts.description: Choose plasmid features such as origin of replication, selectable marker, promoter, and MCS, and interpret bacterial transformation and selection results.

concepts.title: RNA interference knockdown
concepts.description: Design or interpret siRNA/shRNA experiments that trigger RISC-mediated mRNA degradation to reduce gene expression.

concepts.title: Cre-Lox conditional knockout
concepts.description: Predict tissue-specific or inducible gene deletion using Cre recombinase and loxP sites flanking a target exon.

concepts.title: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing
concepts.description: Describe sgRNA targeting, PAM requirement, Cas9 double-strand break formation, and repair by NHEJ or homology-directed repair.

concepts.title: ChIP-seq for protein-DNA interactions
concepts.description: Interpret ChIP-seq peaks as genome-wide binding sites for a transcription factor or histone modification after crosslinking, immunoprecipitation, and sequencing.

concepts.title: Hi-C and 3D genome organization
concepts.description: Interpret Hi-C contact matrices as spatial proximity and identify topologically associating domains and chromatin loops.

concepts.title: RNA-seq and differential expression
concepts.description: Normalize and compare RNA-seq read counts to identify differentially expressed genes between conditions or cell types.
